title: Large duration changes occur with radius-ratio changes in 3,643 Kepler DR24 and DR25 catalog signals
abstract: We compared fitted duration and planet-to-star radius ratio in 3,643 signals with candidate labels in two Kepler catalogs and periods that agree to 0.1 percent. A radius-ratio change greater than a factor of 1.5 occurs in 16 of 37 large-duration-change cases and 113 of 3,606 other cases. The odds ratio is 23.55, with a conditional host-bootstrap 95 percent interval of 11.01 to 47.33. The association persists under stricter quality cuts. The result supports joint parameter checks before physical interpretation of duration flags. Known stellar systems and an older fit of Kepler-160 b illustrate why the flags do not establish new planets or changes with time. Shared photons, fit history, selection, and systematic errors limit the result. No independent telescope observation was tested. The package includes code, a complete derived cohort, 37 flags, exact source hashes, checks, and a figure. Job sci-1107-syam2-astronomy-3c65d5e2868c; machine syam2; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Duration and radius-ratio changes occur together in the selected cohort. Both catalogs use Kepler data.

citations.reason: Uses the same shared catalog sources; adds an individual-signal parameter-change audit.
Prior cross-fit duration work motivates a check of radius-ratio changes.
